$comment: Technique that lives INSIDE a patch. Everything else in this directory is
a whole patch: a structure running from a source to the way out, which a
patch either is or is not. Most of what a technique book teaches is not
that shape. A vibrato that fades in, a lag that turns a jump into a glide,
an envelope that opens loudness and brightness together -- none of them is
a patch, and writing each as one would mean inventing an arbitrary host
and then checking the host instead of the technique.
A fragment carries the same topology in the same words and is asserted by
the same checker. Two rules make it composable rather than a patch with a
piece missing:
1. IT MAY NOT REQUIRE THE AUDIBLE TAIL. 'and it reaches the output' is
the host's business. A fragment claiming it would be unsatisfiable in
every patch that puts anything after it, which is every patch.
2. IT DECLARES ITS SLOT, and the host does not list its fragments. A host
listing what may decorate it is a table that goes stale the first time
somebody adds a fragment and forgets a host -- and the stale entry
looks exactly like 'nothing fits here'.
Both are enforced by `library_problems`, not by convention.
Sources are techniques, not text. Strange's book sets out a taxonomy of
control -- what modulates what, at which rate, through what -- and the
taxonomy is what is derived here, in our words. Nothing is transcribed.
WHAT A FRAGMENT STILL CANNOT SAY. A requirement names the roles at both
ends of one cable. It cannot say 'a DIFFERENT module from the one that
satisfied the last requirement', so 'two unrelated modulators into one
destination' and 'the dry path alongside the wet one' are both out of
reach; where a technique needs that, the fragment here names two different
ROLES instead, which is a weaker claim honestly stated.

idioms.is: A modulator passed through an amplifier that an envelope opens, so the vibrato swells in after the note starts instead of being there from the first instant.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the note begins steady and acquires its waver; the depth grows rather than switching on.
idioms.source: Strange's treatment of modulation depth as itself a controlled quantity

topology.describe: the modulator has to pass through an amplifier — that amplifier IS the depth control
an envelope has to open that amplifier, or the depth is constant and the vibrato is not delayed
the gated modulation has to reach the oscillator, or nothing wavers

listen_for.sounds_like: a note that starts plain and grows a waver, the way a singer or a string player adds vibrato after the attack rather than on it
listen_for.confusable_with: ordinary vibrato, which is present at full depth from the first instant — the difference is entirely in the first half-second

common_mistakes.message: nothing controls the depth, so the vibrato is at full strength from the attack
no modulator passes through the amplifier, so there is nothing to fade in
the gated modulation never reaches a pitch input

idioms.is: The pitch voltage split so it plays the oscillator and opens the filter at once, so a note's colour follows its register instead of every note sharing one cutoff.
idioms.sounds_right_when: high notes are brighter than low ones in the same way an acoustic instrument's are, without the filter audibly sweeping.
idioms.source: Strange on parallel control — one voltage to several destinations

topology.describe: the pitch voltage has to be split, or it can only reach one place
one copy has to play the oscillator
the other copy has to open the filter, which is the whole technique — without it every note has the same colour

listen_for.sounds_like: the top of the range thinner and brighter, the bottom rounder, with no sense that anything is being swept
listen_for.confusable_with: a filter sweep, which moves the colour while a note holds; this one only changes colour when the note does

common_mistakes.message: the pitch never reaches the filter, so bright and dark notes sound identical
the split voltage never reaches a pitch input
nothing feeds the multiple, so there is nothing to track

idioms.is: The pitch voltage passed through a lag before it reaches the oscillator, so a step between notes is travelled rather than jumped.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you hear the journey between two notes, and the destination still arrives cleanly.
idioms.source: Strange on lag processing applied to a control voltage

topology.describe: the pitch voltage has to reach the lag
the LAGGED voltage has to be the one that plays the oscillator — patching the original alongside it defeats the whole thing

listen_for.sounds_like: each note leaning into the next, the pitch audibly in transit for a moment before it settles
listen_for.confusable_with: vibrato, which returns to where it started; a glide arrives somewhere else and stays

common_mistakes.message: the lagged voltage never reaches the oscillator, so the notes still jump
the lag has no pitch voltage to smooth

idioms.is: A modulator routed through an amplifier so a third voltage decides how much of it gets through, which makes the amount of modulation a thing the patch can change while it runs.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the movement is sometimes strong and sometimes absent, without the modulator's rate changing.
idioms.source: Strange's distinction between a modulator and the depth at which it is applied

topology.describe: the modulator has to pass through the amplifier
something has to control that amplifier, or the depth is a knob rather than a voltage
the scaled modulation has to reach a destination

listen_for.sounds_like: motion that comes and goes in strength while keeping the same rate — the pulse of the modulation stays put, its size does not
listen_for.confusable_with: an attenuverter, which sets a depth once; this one keeps changing it

common_mistakes.message: nothing controls the amplifier, so the depth never changes
no modulation passes through the amplifier
the scaled modulation reaches no destination

idioms.is: A periodic modulator and an unpredictable one summed before they reach a destination, so the compound movement never repeats even though half of it does.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you can hear a pulse in the motion and can never quite predict it.
idioms.source: Strange on compound control voltages

topology.describe: a periodic modulator has to reach the summing stage
an unpredictable source has to be summed with it — two periodic sources give a longer cycle, not an open one
the summed voltage has to control something

listen_for.sounds_like: movement with a discernible pulse underneath it that still never lands the same way twice
listen_for.confusable_with: one modulator modulating another, where the rate itself wanders; here both rates are steady and it is the sum that is open

common_mistakes.message: nothing unpredictable is summed in, so the motion repeats on the modulator's cycle
nothing periodic is summed in, so there is no pulse to hear under the drift
the summed modulation controls nothing

implies: one closes as the other opens
idioms.is: One envelope taken to a destination directly and to another through an inverter, so a single gesture opens one thing while closing another.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the two things being controlled trade places rather than moving together.
idioms.source: Strange on inversion as a way of getting two behaviours from one control

topology.describe: the envelope has to control something directly

the same envelope has to reach an attenuverter, which is what CAN invert it — whether it is actually turned past zero is a knob, and no checker reading cables can see it, so this requirement proves the route and not the inversion
the inverted copy has to control something else, or nothing moves the other way

listen_for.sounds_like: a single gesture heard from two sides — as one part swells the other recedes by the same amount and at the same speed
listen_for.confusable_with: two envelopes at different settings, which drift apart; these two are locked, because they are one

common_mistakes.message: nothing inverts the envelope, so both destinations move together
the inverted copy controls nothing
the envelope controls nothing directly, so there is nothing for the inversion to oppose

idioms.is: A function generator whose end-of-cycle fires a second envelope, so one trigger produces a gesture with two stages and a gap the patch decides on.
idioms.sounds_right_when: one event reliably produces two, in the same order, with the delay between them settable.
idioms.source: Strange on cascaded function generators

topology.describe: the first generator's end-of-cycle has to fire a DIFFERENT envelope — a generator whose end-of-cycle retriggers itself is a cycling generator, not a chain, and the two are one cable apart
the second envelope has to control something, or the chain ends in nothing

listen_for.sounds_like: a two-part gesture from one trigger: something happens, a measured pause, then the second thing
listen_for.confusable_with: a single envelope with a long attack, which is one continuous move rather than two separated events

common_mistakes.message: the first generator never fires the second, so there is one stage and not two
the second envelope controls nothing

implies: the envelope opens the filter too
envelope to more than one place
idioms.is: One envelope opening loudness and brightness at once, so a note gets quieter and duller together the way a struck object does.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the decay reads as one gesture: nothing about the note gets brighter as it fades.
idioms.source: Strange on a single control shaping several parameters of one event

topology.describe: the envelope has to control the loudness
the SAME envelope has to move the filter, or a note keeps its colour while it fades

listen_for.sounds_like: notes that go dull as they go quiet, in one motion — the sound of something struck rather than something faded down
listen_for.confusable_with: a separate filter envelope, which can be set to move against the level; this one cannot

common_mistakes.message: the envelope only moves the level, so every note has one colour throughout
the envelope never opens an amplifier, so the note does not articulate

idioms.is: A clocked sequencer taken to a filter rather than to a pitch input, so the pattern is heard as a progression of colours instead of a tune.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the colour steps in time with the clock while the pitch stays put.
idioms.source: Strange on the sequencer as a general control source rather than a note source

topology.describe: the sequencer has to be clocked, or it sits on one step
the sequence has to reach the filter — that is what makes this a timbre sequence rather than a melody

listen_for.sounds_like: a repeating pattern you hear entirely as brightness: same note, stepping colour, locked to the clock
listen_for.confusable_with: a filter sweep, which is continuous; this one moves in discrete steps and lands with the pulse

expect.why: the brightness has to move by more than measurement noise, or the sequence is not reaching the cutoff

common_mistakes.message: nothing clocks the sequencer, so the colour never steps
the sequence never reaches the filter, so nothing sequences the timbre

implies: arpeggio from a sample and hold
idioms.is: A sample-and-hold fed a periodic wave rather than noise, so the held values climb and fall in a pattern that repeats — a staircase, not a scatter.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the pattern is clearly a pattern and clearly repeats, and its length depends on how the two rates sit against each other.
idioms.source: Strange's distinction between sampling noise and sampling a periodic source

topology.describe: a PERIODIC source has to feed the sample-and-hold — feed it noise and the result is random rather than a staircase
a clock has to tell it when to sample
the held voltage has to reach a pitch input

listen_for.sounds_like: a rising or falling run of notes that comes back around, the way an arpeggiator does, but with the pattern length set by two rates rather than by a step count
listen_for.confusable_with: a random sample-and-hold melody, which never comes back around; if you cannot hear the loop, the source is not periodic

expect.why: a staircase with fewer than three treads is not a staircase

common_mistakes.message: nothing clocks the sample-and-hold, so it holds one value
no periodic source feeds it, so there is no repeating staircase
the staircase never reaches a pitch input

idioms.is: A clocked sample-and-hold taken to a filter, so each step lands on a new colour and holds it until the next.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the colour changes in flat steps on the clock, never gliding between them.
idioms.source: Strange on sample-and-hold as a control source for any parameter, not only pitch

topology.describe: a clock has to tell it when to sample
the held voltage has to reach the filter, which is what makes this timbre rather than melody

listen_for.sounds_like: the sound's colour jumping to a new place on every tick and sitting there — flat plateaux, hard edges between them
listen_for.confusable_with: a smoothed random voltage, which drifts between values; if you hear a glide, there is a slew in the way

expect.why: if the brightness barely varies, the held voltage is not reaching the cutoff with any range

common_mistakes.message: nothing clocks the sample-and-hold, so the colour never changes
the held voltage never reaches a filter

idioms.is: An unpredictable voltage passed through a quantizer before it plays anything, so the choice of note is free but the set it is chosen from is not.
idioms.sounds_right_when: you cannot predict the next note and none of them is out of key.
idioms.source: Strange on constraining a random source rather than replacing it

topology.describe: the unpredictable voltage has to reach the quantizer
the QUANTIZED voltage has to be what plays the oscillator, not the raw one

listen_for.sounds_like: notes you cannot anticipate that nonetheless all belong to one scale — surprise without wrongness
listen_for.confusable_with: raw random pitch, which lands between the notes and reads as detuned rather than as a choice

expect.why: a random source constrained to fewer than three notes is a constraint that has swallowed the randomness

common_mistakes.message: the quantizer's output never reaches the oscillator, so the pitches are unconstrained
no random voltage reaches the quantizer

implies: modulate the cutoff at audio rate
idioms.is: An oscillator moving a filter's cutoff fast enough to be heard as pitch rather than as a sweep, which puts sidebands around the filter's own resonance.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the result is clangorous and inharmonic; nothing about it reads as a filter opening.
idioms.source: Strange on the perceptual boundary between a sweep and a sideband

topology.describe: an AUDIO-rate source has to move the cutoff — an LFO here gives a sweep, which is a different technique
audio has to pass through the filter, or there is nothing for the sidebands to form around

listen_for.sounds_like: metallic, unresolved, more like a struck sheet than a filtered tone; the character changes with the ratio of the two frequencies, not with the modulation amount alone
listen_for.confusable_with: a filter sweep, which is the same three jacks at a slower rate — if you hear it open and close, the modulator is below hearing

common_mistakes.message: nothing modulates the cutoff at audio rate
no audio passes through the filter

idioms.is: One oscillator restarting another's cycle, so the second keeps the first's pitch and contributes only its own waveform's shape — the timbre moves when its frequency does, and the pitch does not.
idioms.sounds_right_when: sweeping the synced oscillator changes the colour in hard steps and the note stays put.
idioms.source: The ARP 2600 owner's manual's sync patches; the 2600 normalled this connection and an unnormalled rack has to patch it

topology.describe: one oscillator's output has to land on the OTHER's sync input — a frequency input instead gives FM, which sounds nothing like this

listen_for.sounds_like: a hard, tearing edge on the tone that changes in abrupt steps as the synced oscillator is tuned, with the perceived pitch never moving
listen_for.confusable_with: frequency modulation, where the pitch does move; the giveaway is whether the note wanders when you sweep the modulator

common_mistakes.message: nothing reaches a sync input, so the two oscillators are simply detuned

idioms.is: A slow modulator moving a pulse wave's width, so the harmonic balance shifts continuously and one oscillator acquires the movement of a detuned pair.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the tone thickens and swims without its pitch or its loudness moving at all.
idioms.source: The ARP 2600 owner's manual's pulse-width patches

topology.describe: the modulator has to land on the pulse-width input specifically — the frequency input is vibrato, which is a different sound entirely

listen_for.sounds_like: a single square wave that seems to breathe, gaining and losing body; at the extremes it thins to almost nothing
listen_for.confusable_with: two detuned oscillators, which beat at a rate set by their difference; this one moves at the modulator's rate and stays exactly in tune

common_mistakes.message: nothing modulates the pulse width, so the square wave is static

idioms.is: A stage's output returned to its own input through a summing point, so the signal reprocesses itself and the character depends on how much comes back rather than on any one setting.
idioms.sounds_right_when: small changes in the return amount change the sound out of proportion to the move.
idioms.source: Strange on regeneration in the audio path

topology.describe: the stage's output has to reach a summing point
the sum has to return to that stage's input, or this is an ordinary chain

listen_for.sounds_like: a sound that keeps insisting on itself — resonances build, and the whole thing sits on a knife-edge where a small turn tips it into howling
listen_for.confusable_with: high resonance on a filter, which is bounded; a feedback path is not, and will run away

common_mistakes.message: nothing returns to the input, so there is no feedback
the stage's output never reaches the summing point

idioms.is: High frequencies rolled off before a reverb, so the reverberant share rises as the direct sound dulls and the source reads as further away rather than merely quieter.
idioms.sounds_right_when: it sits back in the picture; turning it up does not bring it forward.
idioms.source: Strange on the cues that place a sound in a space

topology.describe: the signal has to lose its top before it is placed
the dulled signal has to reach a reverb, or there is no space to be far away in

listen_for.sounds_like: something heard across a room: soft edges, more room than source, and it stays back when you raise the level
listen_for.confusable_with: simply turning it down, which keeps the sound near and small

common_mistakes.message: nothing rolls off the top, so the sound reads as near and quiet rather than distant
the dulled signal never reaches a reverb

implies: make an envelope from a gate
idioms.is: A gate passed through a lag so its edges become a rise and a fall, which is an envelope generator made from a slew limiter and nothing else.
idioms.sounds_right_when: notes fade in and out at a rate you set, rather than switching on and off.
idioms.source: Strange on the lag processor used as a function generator

topology.describe: a gate has to reach the lag — the lag's rate is the attack and the decay
the rounded voltage has to open an amplifier, or nothing is shaped by it

listen_for.sounds_like: soft-edged notes with symmetrical rise and fall — the attack and the release are the same speed, which is the tell that a lag made them
listen_for.confusable_with: a proper envelope generator, whose attack and decay are set separately and are usually not equal

common_mistakes.message: no gate reaches the lag, so there are no edges to round
the rounded voltage opens nothing

idioms.is: Noise taken to an oscillator's frequency input, so the pitch is never quite still and the tone acquires a roughness that no periodic modulator produces.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the note is recognisably one note and audibly unsteady, with no rate you can count.
idioms.source: Strange on noise used as a control source rather than as a sound

topology.describe: noise has to reach the oscillator's frequency input — this is noise as a CONTROL, not as a sound

forbidden_topology.describe: the noise source must not also be what plays the note — a sampled voltage on the 1V/octave jack is a melody, and this library's `cv_in` deliberately includes that jack, so without this the two are the same requirement

listen_for.sounds_like: a growl or a rasp riding on the note; the pitch centre holds while the edges refuse to settle
listen_for.confusable_with: vibrato, which has a countable rate; if you can tap along with the wobble it is not noise doing it

common_mistakes.message: no noise reaches the oscillator, so the pitch is perfectly steady
the noise source is what plays the note, so this is a random melody rather than a roughened tone

idioms.is: A clock combined with an unpredictable gate through logic, so hits land on the pulse but not on every one of them.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the rhythm is unmistakably in time and never the same bar twice.
idioms.source: Strange on logic as a way of conditioning one gate stream with another

topology.describe: the pulse has to reach the logic, or the result is not in time
an unpredictable gate has to decide which pulses survive
what gets through has to trigger something

listen_for.sounds_like: a pattern locked to the grid with holes punched in it — every hit is where it should be, and which ones happen keeps changing
listen_for.confusable_with: an unmetered random rhythm, where the hits themselves drift off the grid

common_mistakes.message: nothing decides which pulses survive, so every beat plays
no clock reaches the logic, so the surviving hits are not in time
the surviving gates trigger nothing

idioms.is: A divided clock restarting a sequencer's cycle, so the pattern's length is set by the reset rather than by the sequencer's own step count.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the phrase repeats at a length that is not the sequencer's, and lands on the same step every time.
idioms.source: Strange on sequential controllers and the control of their cycle length

topology.describe: the sequencer still has to be clocked, or there is nothing to reset
a divided clock has to reach the sequencer's reset, which is what shortens the phrase

listen_for.sounds_like: a pattern that turns over before it has finished, so a sixteen-step sequence played in sevens keeps starting again mid-phrase
listen_for.confusable_with: a polymetric sequence, where two patterns of different lengths run free against each other and only realign occasionally

common_mistakes.message: nothing resets the sequencer, so the phrase is just its own step count
the sequencer is never clocked

implies: modulation in time with the clock
idioms.is: A divided clock restarting a modulator's cycle, so the movement lines up with the pulse instead of drifting against it.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the modulation lands on the beat every time rather than wandering in and out of phase.
idioms.source: Strange on synchronising a control source to a timing source

topology.describe: the pulse has to be divided to the rate the modulation should lock to
the division has to restart the modulator, or it free-runs and drifts against the pulse

listen_for.sounds_like: movement that breathes exactly with the music and arrives at the same point every bar
listen_for.confusable_with: a free-running modulator set close to the right rate, which drifts — audible over a minute, not over four bars

common_mistakes.message: nothing restarts the modulator, so it drifts against the pulse
no clock reaches the divider

implies: change the shape of the modulation
idioms.is: A control voltage passed through a non-linear stage before it reaches its destination, so a straight ramp arrives as a curve and the movement is no longer evenly paced.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the motion lingers at one end of its travel and hurries through the other.
idioms.source: Strange on non-linear processing applied to control rather than to audio

topology.describe: the control voltage has to pass through the shaping stage
the SHAPED voltage has to be what reaches the destination, or the bend changes nothing

listen_for.sounds_like: a sweep that is no longer even — it hangs at the top and falls away quickly, or the reverse, from a modulator that has not changed rate
listen_for.confusable_with: an attenuator, which changes how far the movement goes but not how it is paced

common_mistakes.message: the shaped voltage reaches no destination, so the original curve is what arrives
no control voltage reaches the shaping stage

idioms.is: One filter feeding another, so the slopes add and a band can be narrowed further than either stage could narrow it alone.
idioms.sounds_right_when: the rejected part of the spectrum is gone rather than merely reduced.
idioms.source: Strange on cascaded filtering

topology.describe: a source has to reach the first filter
the first filter's output has to feed a SECOND filter — side by side they sum, and summing is a different technique

listen_for.sounds_like: a much narrower, more definite band than one filter gives; sweeping it reads as a focused resonance travelling rather than a broad curtain moving
listen_for.confusable_with: two filters in parallel, which produces two bands at once — the formant technique, not this one

common_mistakes.message: the filters are not in series, so the slopes never add
nothing feeds the first filter
